gold_assessment.reasoning: Gold: chief complaint is anxiety symptoms. Generated CC-001 includes anxiety but adds morning distress about leaving the house, sleep disturbance, and palpitations; there is no generated fact that simply states the chief complaint as anxiety symptoms alone.
Gold: two‑month history of feeling anxious all the time. Generated HPI-001: anxiety for approximately two months. Duration and ongoing anxiety are captured, with additional job detail.

Gold: anxiety began after starting a new job in a different industry with pressure from boss. Generated HPI-001: onset with a new stressful job at a fashion retailer. Start of anxiety after new job and work stress are captured, but ‘different industry’ and ‘pressure from boss’ are omitted.
Gold: dreads going to work every morning. Generated HPI-002: dreads going to work; anticipatory worry. Morning aspect not restated but dread of going to work is clearly covered.

Gold: severe initial insomnia taking about 3 hours to fall asleep. Generated HPI-004: difficulty falling asleep; HPI-005: total sleep 3–4 hours, but does not specify it takes 3 hours to fall asleep. Severity and exact 3‑hour latency are omitted.
Gold: early-morning waking. Generated facts describe difficulty falling asleep and waking with racing heart/fear of being late but do not clearly indicate early‑morning waking as a pattern.
Gold: often only 3–4 hours sleep. Generated HPI-005: sleeps about 3–4 hours. Matches.
Gold: tired during the day. Generated ASM-002: insomnia with daytime fatigue. Daytime fatigue corresponds to tired in the day.
Gold: reports low energy. Generated HPI-010 and ROS-003: low energy. Direct match.
Gold: eating pattern normal but more chocolate. No generated fact addresses eating pattern or increased chocolate intake.

Gold: anhedonia at work and outside; previously enjoyed running, tennis, socialising; now often avoids. Generated HPI-009, HPI-011, HPI-012, PE-004, ROS-003 describe low mood, anhedonia, reduced interest, social withdrawal, decreased hobbies/exercise, but specific prior activities (running, tennis, socialising) and the nuance ‘now still sees friends but often avoids’ are not stated.

Gold: palpitations began with anxiety symptoms. Generated HPI-007, PE-001, ROS-001 describe palpitations features but do not explicitly state onset coinciding with start of anxiety. Timing-onset relationship is omitted.

Gold: palpitations feel irregular and are accompanied by chest discomfort. Generated HPI-007 and HPI-008 / ROS-001: irregular, fast heartbeat with occasional brief chest discomfort when heart is racing. Fully aligns.

Gold: palpitations are rapid and last approximately 2–10 minutes. Generated HPI-007 / PE-001 / ROS-001: irregular, fast heartbeat with episodes lasting minutes to about 10 minutes. Rate and upper duration are captured, but explicit lower bound of 2 minutes is not repeated; still essentially covered, but not verbatim.
Gold: patient has not missed work despite symptoms. No generated fact comments on work attendance or not missing work.
Gold: public transport is a trigger for anxiety. No generated fact mentions public transport as an anxiety‑provoking factor.
Gold: low mood most of the time. Generated HPI-009 and ROS-003: distressed, low mood. While ‘most of the time’ is not repeated, persistent low mood is implied and reasonably covered.
Gold: no past psychiatric history or significant anxiety. Generated PMH-001 simply says PMH not documented; this conflicts by omission, so the specific negative psych history is not captured.
Gold: mother has a history of depression. Generated FH-001 says family history not documented, so the specific maternal depression is missing.
Gold: lives with supportive parents. Generated SH-005 and SH-006: lives with parents; supportive family; good support system. The fact that the family are parents and supportive is covered.

Gold: drinks Friday/Saturday, amount uncertain but sometimes overdoes it. Generated SH-002: heavier alcohol use on Fridays and Saturdays. Pattern and heavier use covered; uncertainty of amount and ‘sometimes overdoes it’ nuance approximated but not exact.
Gold: smokes occasionally. Generated SH-003 and PE-005: occasional smoking. Direct match.
Gold: does not use illicit drugs. Generated SH-004 and PE-005: no illicit drugs reported. Matches.

Gold: work-related anxiety. Generated ASM-001 and ASM-005: anxiety disorder related to work stress and occupational stressor (new job). Work‑related nature is covered, though ‘work-related anxiety’ is embedded in a broader anxiety disorder description.
Gold: insomnia. Generated ASM-002: insomnia with daytime fatigue and anhedonia. Insomnia is clearly included.
Gold: advised self‑referral to NHS talking therapies. Generated PLAN-001: self‑refer to NHS talking therapies; same content with extra detail about CBT types and link.

Gold: advised to access online CBT resources, info attached. Generated PLAN-002: online resources for anxiety management with review/escalation; PLAN-010: send/attach information on sleep and anxiety management. Access to online resources and sending info are covered; explicit ‘online CBT’ wording is generalized to ‘anxiety management’ and ‘sleep/anxiety’ materials.

Gold: blood tests as initial investigation for palpitations, patient to book via support team. Generated PLAN-004: arrange basic blood tests to evaluate contributors to palpitations. Indication and test type are covered, but the instruction to book via support team is omitted.

Gold: contact clinic for further discussion if anxiety/mood worse or unable to cope with work. Generated PLAN-002 adds review if no improvement or worsening and PLAN-007/FU‑002 discuss contacting GP/urgent care for chest pain/fainting/suicidality. However, there is no explicit instruction matching ‘contact us if mood/anxiety worse or unable to cope with work’; thus only partially aligned on the ‘worsening’ concept.
Gold: no panic attacks. No generated fact states absence of panic attacks.
Gold: denies suicidal ideation. Generated HPI-014 and ROS-003: no suicidal thoughts; no suicidality. Fully matches.

gen_assessment.reasoning: Gold CC only states anxiety symptoms. Added details of morning distress about leaving the house, sleep disturbance, and palpitations as part of the chief complaint are not in gold and do not contradict.
Duration (~2 months) matches gold HPI-001. Added specifics (fashion retailer, described as stressful) are not in gold but consistent with gold HPI-002’s new job with pressures from boss.
Dreading going to work is supported by gold HPI-003. ‘Anticipatory worry about performing well’ is an extrapolation not present in gold but consistent, so considered an addition.

Gold describes anxiety impacting sleep and various daily functions (insomnia, low energy, anhedonia, social avoidance). Summarizing as impacting sleep and daily life is consistent with multiple gold HPI facts.
Difficulty falling asleep is supported by severe initial insomnia in gold HPI-004. Bedtime 22:00–23:00 is not documented in gold, so it is an addition.
Total sleep time 3–4 hours is supported by gold HPI-006. ‘Non‑restorative sleep’ is not explicitly in gold but is compatible with tiredness and low energy; treated as addition.
Gold notes insomnia and palpitations but does not state waking with racing heart or fear of being late. These are new details, not contradicted but not present.
Irregular, fast heartbeat and episodes lasting minutes to ~10 minutes with chest discomfort are all supported by gold HPI-012 and HPI-013.
Occasional brief chest discomfort when the heart is racing aligns with gold chest discomfort associated with palpitations.
Distressed, low mood, anhedonia, and reduced interest in activities are supported by gold descriptions of low mood, anhedonia, and avoidance of previously enjoyed activities.
Low energy is explicitly documented in gold.

Gold describes ‘now still sees friends but often avoids’; generated describes social withdrawal and avoidance of friends. This elaborates the pattern; it is consistent but more absolute than gold, so partially supported with additive nuance.
Decreased participation in hobbies/exercise corresponds to avoiding previously enjoyed running and tennis.
Difficulty engaging in evening activities because of stress is not mentioned in gold; it is a new functional detail.
No suicidal thoughts equals denied suicidal ideation in gold.
Statement that no vitals, exam findings, or labs are documented is a meta-comment about the transcript, not present in gold clinical facts. It does not contradict gold.
Generated: past medical history not documented. Gold PMH-001 explicitly documents no past psychiatric history/significant anxiety, so PMH is in fact documented (at least psych).
Gold has no information on current medications. Saying medications are not documented is an added meta-statement; not contradicted by gold.
Gold has no allergy information. Stating allergies not documented is an added meta-observation, not contradicted.
Generated: family history not specifically documented. Gold FH-001 clearly documents maternal depression, so family history is documented.

Gold implies the patient has a job; SH-001 specifying full‑time head office work adds detail but is consistent. Treated as addition on top of being broadly supported by the presence of a job as a stressor.
Heavier alcohol use on Fridays/Saturdays aligns with gold description of drinking those days and sometimes overdoing it.
Occasional smoking matches gold ‘smokes occ’.
No illicit drug use reported matches gold ‘no illicit drugs’.
Lives with parents is directly in gold.
Supportive family/good support system aligns with ‘lives with supportive parents’.

Gold: work-related anxiety. Generated expands to ‘anxiety disorder with somatic symptoms causing functional impairment (work stress, social withdrawal)’. Work-related anxiety portion is supported; the formal ‘disorder’ framing and detailed functional impairments are additions.

Insomnia is supported in gold. Association with daytime fatigue and anhedonia is consistent with gold HPI-007, HPI-008, HPI-010 but not explicitly tied by the clinician as part of the insomnia assessment; thus partly additive.

Gold notes low mood most of the time and absence of suicidality. Framing as ‘depressed mood in context of anxiety; no suicidality’ is conceptually consistent but goes beyond gold’s wording; partially supported with added diagnostic framing.

Gold only notes palpitations and that blood tests will investigate them; it does not state they are likely anxiety-related or to consider evaluation for organic causes. This reasoning is new but not contradicted.
Gold: new job with pressures from boss associated with onset of anxiety. Generated: new job as occupational stressor contributing to symptom severity. Fully consistent.
Self-referral to NHS talking therapies is exactly in gold; mention of CBT/behavioral therapies and providing a link are additions.

Gold: access online CBT resources, info attached. Generated: online resources for anxiety management, review if no improvement or worsening, consider escalation. The ‘online resources’ portion is supported; the explicit follow-up/escalation plan is additional.
Gold does not mention reassurance, sleep hygiene counseling, or specific advice on sleep schedule/caffeine/screen use. These are new plan elements.
Gold: blood test as initial investigation for palpitations. Generated: arrange basic blood tests to evaluate contributors to palpitations. Equivalent.
Gold only states that blood tests are advised and booked via support team; no timing or GP follow-up is documented. Generated 1‑week GP follow-up is new.
No gold fact about medication discussions. This is a new consideration.

Gold follow-up is about contacting the clinic if mood/anxiety worse or unable to cope with work; there is no mention of instructions re chest pain, fainting, or increasing suicidality. New safety advice.
Gold documents alcohol use pattern but not any counseling to reduce it. Counseling and identifying it as contributor are new.

Gold notes the patient now often avoids socialising and activities. Encouraging social contact and re‑engagement is a logical but undocumented recommendation; content is consistent but not stated by gold, so this is additive despite being related.

Gold: attached info for online CBT. Generated: send/attach information on sleep and anxiety management. The act of sending/attaching info is supported; the exact scope (sleep + anxiety vs CBT) is broader and somewhat different, thus partly additive.
Gold follow‑up only specifies contacting clinic if symptoms worsen or unable to cope with work. No scheduled 1‑week GP follow‑up after tests is documented; this is new.
Instructions to seek urgent/GP review for chest pain, fainting, or increasing suicidality are not present in gold. This is new safety guidance.

Irregular fast heartbeat lasting minutes to ~10 minutes matches gold palpitations description. However, in gold this is from history, not an objective physical finding; conceptually supported but sectioning differs.
Gold supports poor sleep duration and difficulty falling asleep; nocturnal awakenings due to anxiety/palpitations are not explicitly described and are an addition.
Distress, low mood, anhedonia, and low energy are supported by multiple gold HPI facts (low mood, anhedonia, low energy).
Social withdrawal and reduced engagement in activities are consistent with gold noting anhedonia and avoidance of previously enjoyed running, tennis, and socialising.
Likely increased weekend alcohol, occasional smoking, and no illicit drugs mirror gold SH-002 to SH-004, with ‘likely’ as interpretive but consistent.
Cardiovascular ROS description of palpitations and chest discomfort is directly supported by gold palpitations description.
Difficulty falling asleep and short total duration (3–4 hours) are supported by gold HPI-004 and HPI-006. ‘Non‑restorative sleep’ and waking with racing heart/fear of being late are additions.

Anxiety, low mood, anhedonia, reduced interest, low energy, and absence of suicidal thoughts are all supported by various gold HPI/ROS facts. Grouping them as a structured psychiatric ROS is consistent but somewhat broader than explicitly given; overall supported with minor additive structuring.
